findings.issue: The generic pokemonCards helper carries an extra callback and Card.hidden (lib/types.ts:9, PokemonCards.tsx:23) that exist only for the Abilities feature, entangling a shared abstraction with one route.
findings.suggestion: Let the ability route decorate its own cards (or pass an optional render-extra per list) and keep hidden-ability text out of the shared Card type and component.

findings.issue: The pre-hydration input-replay effect plus ref-sync effect is a subtle pattern duplicated in pokemon.tsx:205-212 for the game select; changes to hydration behavior must be applied twice and are easy to get wrong.
findings.suggestion: Extract a small shared hook (e.g. useSyncedSelect) or switch to controlled inputs driven by loaderData so the sync logic exists once.

findings.issue: MoveRow is a loader-built data shape exported from a presentational component and imported by routes/pokemon.tsx:13, blurring the data/UI boundary.
findings.suggestion: Move MoveRow to app/app/lib/types.ts next to Card and TypeInfo.

findings.issue: The server module has no 'server-only' import guard; a future client-side import would silently misbehave (process.env-based URL, module-level cache shipped to the browser) instead of failing the build.
findings.suggestion: Add `import 'server-only'` (or an equivalent vite alias) so misuse fails at build time.

findings.issue: The splat not-found route's loader throws the exact 404 that the root ErrorBoundary (root.tsx:76-78) already renders for unmatched URLs, so the extra route file mostly duplicates framework behavior.
findings.suggestion: Either drop routes/not-found.tsx and rely on the root ErrorBoundary's 404 branch, or keep it but document why; today the two paths can drift.

findings.issue: URL query serialization is built ad hoc here (queryString) and inline in pokemon.tsx:180 (?game=), so a change to query handling touches two hand-rolled builders.
findings.suggestion: One shared helper (or URLSearchParams consistently) for building search strings.

findings.issue: speciesCard's withTypes boolean is mild flag creep with only two call sites (home wants types, the other lists don't).
findings.suggestion: Acceptable as-is; if a third variant appears, split into explicit builders instead of adding more flags.

summary: A tidy, current React Router v8 framework-mode app: all API access, caching and card construction sit in one server module, so data-source and card-level changes are one-file fixes. Components are dumb prop-driven primitives and the abstractions (pokemonCards, MoveTable's column config) stretch to the real variation in the app. The main friction is small: an ability-specific 'hidden' flag threaded through shared card code, and a subtle pre-hydration input-replay pattern duplicated across two routes.
